mainText:
A magnitude five point nine level election campaign crisis deepened overnight, with New Zealand's Chief of Defence gone and enrolments now closed ahead of polling day.

New Zealand.

Enrolments for the election closed at midnight, with around three hundred thousand people still unenrolled when the deadline hit. Young people aged eighteen to twenty four made up nearly half of that group. Christopher Luxon and Chris Hipkins both urged last minute enrolment before the deadline. Advance voting has now begun.

Air Marshal Tony Davies has resigned as Chief of Defence over what Defence Minister Judith Collins called an inappropriate relationship. Reported by RNZ and Newsroom. National has removed a campaign volunteer after learning of a conviction for sexual conduct with a minor, with Christopher Luxon saying he was glad the party acted swiftly. The gang photo row continues, with Luxon defending minister Potaka and arguing not all gang photos are equivalent, while Hipkins accuses National of double standards.

National has released a twenty six point one hundred day plan if re elected, compiling existing campaign commitments. A commentator told RNZ the left bloc has lost control of the campaign in its final week, saying Labour can no longer blame its allies for the gang scandal.

In Tauranga, a woman's body has been found in a Kawerau house after a train hit a car, with police launching a homicide investigation into what they call a suspicious death. In Western Bay of Plenty, Alan Kurtovich has confirmed his resignation as a councillor, which triggered the current byelection, was because of the district's Māori wards decision. He says it was still the right call.

Oil prices have hit their highest level since May on reports the United States is again weighing strikes on Iran, with the Reserve Bank's Official Cash Rate decision due this week, widely expected to rise by twenty five basis points.

World.

Elon Musk has confirmed SpaceX restricted Ukraine's use of Starlink, accusing Ukraine's military of violating the service's terms by using it for offensive drone strikes. Ukraine has rejected the claim as strange. Service has since been restored. Reported by BBC and Stuff.

More than one thousand three hundred people have been arrested across France after another day of mass protests, with demonstrations also spreading to other European countries. Reported by BBC.

Serbia is reporting record high turnout in elections being watched as the strongest challenge yet to President Aleksandar Vučić's twelve year rule, driven by a student protest movement. Reported by BBC and Stuff.

A second patient, a sixty five year old woman, has died of Ebola in Kenya, a close family member of the first victim who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo. Uganda has ordered a twenty one day quarantine for citizens returning from Congo as a precaution, despite declaring itself Ebola free. Reported by BBC and Al Jazeera.

Technology.

A critical flaw in the PHP programming language, used across much of the internet, continues to trigger a global security scramble days after discovery. The UK government says five hundred new vulnerabilities have been found in its own systems, and Amazon has reported attacks before the flaw was made public. Researchers say artificial intelligence helped uncover the issue, described as among the most significant ever found. The practical cyber event is still expected, not yet realised. Reported by BBC Technology, now into its third day of coverage.

Sport.

League. Rugby League World Cup. The Kiwis beat the Cook Islands eighty two to sixteen in Christchurch, a matter of record. The Kiwi Ferns beat France ninety two to nil in the women's tournament. Samoa's men stay unbeaten, setting up next weekend's clash with Tonga in Sydney. Australia beat Fiji thirty six to twenty two to reach the semi finals with a pool match to spare. Police have again asked fans to keep victory celebrations within reasonable hours after further complaints about late night parades. The Australian Rugby League is standing firm on keeping the PNG Chiefs name despite New Zealand Rugby's legal challenge.

Netball. The Silver Ferns have won the Constellation Cup for just the fourth time, fighting back in the final quarter against Australia. Coach Dame Noeline Taurua says the team is coming of age. They are now one win away from the world number one ranking.

Rugby. All Blacks forwards Shannon Frizell, Tyrel Lomax and Samisoni Taukei'aho remain ruled out of the upcoming United Kingdom tour with leg and neck injuries.

Cricket. India beat the Black Caps by four wickets in the second Twenty20, taking a two nil series lead, a matter of record.

Football. Manchester United lost nil to three at home to Bournemouth, leaving them winless in eight Premier League games. Manager Michael Carrick says his future is under major threat and admits he does not know if he will survive. Auckland FC conceded five goals in a loss to Western Sydney, their first defeat under new coach Pedro Moreira.

Athletics. Legendary coach Arch Jelley, who guided John Walker to Olympic mile gold, has died aged one hundred and four.

Coming up. The Reserve Bank's Official Cash Rate decision lands this week. The Rugby League World Cup semi finals approach, with Samoa facing Tonga in Sydney next weekend. Election day is November the seventh.

End of flash.
